snapshots.title: Same displacement, different velocity
snapshots.alt: Maz and Eli each walk six meters east. Maz takes six seconds and Eli takes twelve. Maz averages one meter per second east; Eli averages half a meter per second east.
snapshots.body: Both walkers reach the same endpoint. Their elapsed times differ.
snapshots.question: Why does the same displacement produce different average velocities?

snapshots.title: A round trip still includes motion
snapshots.alt: The notebook shows six meters east and six west in twelve seconds. Average speed is one meter per second and average velocity is zero.
snapshots.body: The route has 12 m of distance and zero displacement over 12 s.
snapshots.question: Which measurements would reveal the motion that the zero average velocity hides?
snapshots.work: Part 2 · Collect and check your trials

snapshots.title: Walk the graph, then explain it
snapshots.alt: A position–time graph joins zero seconds and one meter, four seconds and five meters, six seconds and five meters, then ten seconds and one meter.
snapshots.body: The rising, flat and falling segments tell different parts of the trip.
snapshots.question: How can +1, 0 and −1 m/s describe the segments while the whole-trip average is zero?
snapshots.work: Part 3 · Defend the whole motion story
